title: Read request cookies on the server
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed app/preferences/page.tsx change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Set light, dark and unknown theme cookies and inspect rendered text.
Confirm the client bundle contains no next/headers import.
Repeat with Cache Components explicitly enabled and add the required runtime boundary.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: next/headers is a server request API, not a client storage library.
Set light, dark and unknown theme cookies and inspect rendered text.
alternativeApproaches: A display preference is not an identity proof. Authentication cookies need integrity, secure attributes, expiry and server-side verification; never trust a role string merely because it arrived in a cookie.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.

verification: Set light, dark and unknown theme cookies and inspect rendered text.
Confirm the client bundle contains no next/headers import.
Repeat with Cache Components explicitly enabled and add the required runtime boundary.
nextjsPractice.next15: cookies() is asynchronous; synchronous access is temporary compatibility, not a stable pattern.
nextjsPractice.next16: Await cookies(). With Cache Components enabled, read request data in a runtime subtree behind Suspense instead of inside use cache.
